verdict.reason: speed >= 15.000 m/s was sustained for 0.000 s; 1.000 s was required
verdict.conclusion: The explicit 60 km/h target reaches planning and the command gate. Repeated curvature-derived speed caps and negative trajectory feed-forward interrupt acceleration on a geometrically straight route; when acceleration is permitted, the 1.5 m/s^2 controller/gate envelope and 0.4 throttle clamp expose a large map-to-plant response mismatch. Raising max_throttle to 0.5 alone is a useful isolated simulation probe, but is not supported as sufficient to reach 15 m/s.

model_or_target_velocity.note: The raw VAD velocity remains evidence only; the simulation-only explicit nominal overlay owns the cruise target.

controller_effect.at_16_sec: trajectory target about 7.51 m/s and -2.0 m/s^2 feed-forward reduced a saturated P+I request to about 0.16 m/s^2
controller_effect.at_42_sec: trajectory target about 10.48 m/s and -2.0 m/s^2 feed-forward produced about -0.15 m/s^2 before downstream limiting while actual speed was about 8.17 m/s

conditioned_trajectory_curvature.note: The route itself is effectively straight. The speed cap matches sqrt(maximum_lateral_acceleration / peak_curvature), so mid-route reductions are caused by conditioned trajectory geometry rather than terminal stopping distance.

longitudinal_controller_and_command_gate.note: The limit is intentional and safe, but it prevents the controller from asking the converter for materially more than 1.5 m/s^2 during the available acceleration windows.

command_application_cross_check.interpretation: The interface generally applies the converter output; the shortfall is not explained by command transport loss.

throttle_cap_and_actuation_calibration.note: At the existing 1.5 m/s^2 request, opening the 0.5 row raises the calculated command only from 0.4 to at most about 0.415. The binned comparison is an observational mismatch signal, not a substitute for a dedicated steady-state actuation calibration run.

actuation_map_velocity_axis.note: The v3 run never reached the map boundary. If speed later exceeds 13.89 m/s, lookups clamp to the final velocity column, so the map must be extended and calibrated before claiming 60 km/h readiness.

route_length.note: The 445.88 m route is ample for the configured acceleration/deceleration model. With the observed high-speed acceleration response and repeated curvature slowdowns it becomes too short, but extending the route would mask rather than fix the control/calibration causes.

recommended_next_steps.change: Use the existing --tight-corridor profile (route corridor half-width 0.5 m to 0.2 m) with all speed, controller, gate, map, and throttle settings unchanged.
recommended_next_steps.purpose: Test whether suppressing VAD-conditioned lateral excursions removes the false curvature caps while retaining curvature safety logic.
acceptance_focus: planning horizon no longer develops mid-route 4-9 m/s caps on the physical straight
conditioned trajectory p95 peak curvature materially decreases toward <= 0.00444 1/m for a 15 m/s cap at 1.0 m/s^2
recommended_next_steps.risk: A tighter hard corridor can introduce clipping kinks or reduce VAD geometry fidelity; reject if peak curvature or correction increases.

recommended_next_steps.change: After geometry behavior is isolated, version a simulation-only raw converter config with max_throttle 0.4 to 0.5 and no other change.
recommended_next_steps.purpose: Measure the contribution of the existing 0.4 clamp using the already present 0.5 accel-map row.
recommended_next_steps.expected_scope: diagnostic A/B only; not expected to be sufficient for 15 m/s because the present 1.5 m/s^2 request resolves to at most 0.415 throttle in v3
recommended_next_steps.risk: Higher CARLA throttle can increase overshoot and lateral acceleration; keep the 18 m/s maximum-speed abort and simulation-only provenance.

recommended_next_steps.change: Collect steady-state CARLA pedal/speed/acceleration sweeps, extend the velocity axis beyond 16.67 m/s with margin, then version the map and any controller/gate envelope change together as an explicitly exploratory profile.
recommended_next_steps.purpose: Correct the observed map-to-plant mismatch before another 60 km/h qualification attempt.
recommended_next_steps.risk: Do not transfer the resulting CARLA calibration or 60 km/h settings to a real vehicle; separate real-vehicle calibration and safety validation are required.

rejected_shortcuts.change: Disable the trajectory curvature speed cap
rejected_shortcuts.reason: At 15 m/s, curvature 0.02 1/m implies about 4.5 m/s^2 lateral acceleration, far above the 1.2 m/s^2 trial limit.
This hides conditioned-geometry and calibration defects and does not make the actuation map valid beyond its 13.89 m/s axis.
The offline inverse-map calculation shows only a 0.015 maximum command increment under the current 1.5 m/s^2 envelope.

calculation_method.time_basis: ROS message/header stamps; planning time is relative to the first /planning/trajectory header stamp
calculation_method.bag_access: rosbag2 sequential read-only deserialization; no playback and no ROS graph mutation
calculation_method.curvature: signed three-point Menger curvature kappa = 2*cross(AB,AC)/(|AB|*|BC|*|AC|); speed cap = sqrt(maximum_lateral_acceleration_mps2/abs(kappa)); this matches trajectory_planar_curvatures() and limit_trajectory_speed_for_curvature() in the preserved route-manager source
calculation_method.map_inverse: For each gated-control sample, linearly interpolate every accel-map throttle row over absolute odometry speed, then linearly interpolate throttle over requested acceleration exactly as AccelMap::getThrottle does; compare the result with the 0.4 config clamp
calculation_method.response_bins: Nearest header-stamp alignment of gated control, odometry, actuation command, and robust measured acceleration; retain positive requested acceleration, brake < 0.001, throttle >= 0.25; group by actual-speed bins. No response-delay correction is applied, so the result is used only as a mismatch signal.
calculation_method.route_distance_check: constant-acceleration relation d=(v2^2-v1^2)/(2*a); the 0.165 m/s^2 extrapolation is explicitly illustrative and not a plant model
